# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

I see the bomb display and Blind just gestured to me with 🖐 (open hand, five fingers). Since I can't hear anyone, gestures from Blind are my only input from them. I need to relay what I see to Mute (who can hear me) since Blind can't perceive my speech or gestures directly—wait, actually let me check: I speak and both Mute and Blind receive it. So I can tell both at once.

Let me report the bomb state clearly. The gesture 🖐 from Blind might be an attempt to signal something, but without prior context I shouldn't assume too much. I should just report what I see plainly so Mute (who has the manual) can start giving instructions.

```
speak(text="Display reads zero. Light is green. Button is large, labeled push to defeat. Wires are three: one green, two yellow, three red.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍 👎 👆]

Let me think about this. Mute just gestured to me: ☝ 👍 👎 👆. Mute can't speak, only gesture, and gestures carry no words—just symbols. Mute has the manual and is trying to communicate something to me using only these hand symbols, likely to ask me something or confirm/deny a hypothesis about the wires or button.

☝ (index finger up) could mean "one" or "wire 1". 👍 could mean "yes/correct". 👎 could mean "no/incorrect". 👆 (pointing up) could also relate to a specific item.

This might be Mute trying to ask me a question like "is it wire 1? yes or no" but I can't respond to gestures with gestures in a way Mute can interpret without more established meaning. Actually wait - I CAN gesture, and Mute CAN see gestures (Mute is not deaf, just can't speak). Let me re-check the rules: Mute reads the manual. Mute's cannot: speak, touch bomb. So Mute can presumably see and hear? Let's check the table again - only listed cannots are speak/touch. So Mute can see and hear.

So Mute is asking me something via gesture, possibly "is wire 1 green? yes/no" - ☝ = wire 1, 👍/👎 = yes/no options, 👆 = pointing at something above (the button?).

I should respond with gestures since Mute can see. Let me confirm wire 1 is green with a gesture back, and also use speech to give full detail since Blind also receives my speech but not gestures.

```
speak(text="Confirming again for anyone listening: wire one is green, wire two is yellow, wire three is red. Display shows zero, light is green, button says push to defuse.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍 🖐 👎]

Let me think through this. Mute gestured ☝ 👍 🖐 👎 to me. My previous gesture reply was ☝ 👍 (confirming wire 1 is green). Now Mute responds with ☝ 👍 🖐 👎.

This could mean: "wire 1 - yes (confirmed), 🖐 (five/hand - maybe referring to Blind, or asking about something else) - no". Or it could be building a sequence: ☝👍 = wire1 confirmed good, then 🖐👎 = something with five (maybe the button?) is a no.

Actually, 🖐 was the gesture Blind sent me last turn too. Maybe 🖐 is being used as a symbol meaning "Blind" or "the button" (five fingers = push?). Given Blind gestured 🖐 to me, and now Mute gestures 🖐 too, this could be a symbol they've agreed represents something specific - perhaps "wait" or "stop" or "the big button".

Since I can't ask clarifying questions via gesture easily (no back-and-forth confirmation protocol established), I should stick to speaking plainly what I see, since that's my most reliable channel to both Mute and Blind. I'll also try mirroring back to acknowledge receipt.

```
speak(text="Repeating full picture: display zero, light green, wires one green two yellow three red, large button says push to defuse. No changes since last turn.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐", "👎"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👎]

Mute is sending two separate gesture messages this turn: ☝ 👍 and 🖐 👎. This looks like Mute is confirming/echoing back what I sent last turn split into two separate calls - possibly confirming "wire 1: yes" and "five (button?): no" as a readback check, or Mute is establishing a protocol where they send back what they understood to verify.

Given the pattern - I sent ☝👍 (wire1 = good/cut?) and 🖐👎 (button = don't push) in one message, and now Mute echoes back the same two pairs as separate messages - this looks like acknowledgment/confirmation of receipt.

Since nothing on the board has changed, and Mute seems to be confirming understanding, I should continue being consistent. Let me try to establish clearer meaning - perhaps I should propose: wire 1 = safe (cut it), and button = do NOT push. Let me try encoding a clearer instruction now, since Mute may be waiting for me to make a decision/recommendation given I have full visual info and Mute has the manual.

Actually - Mute has the manual, so Mute should be telling ME what to do, or telling Blind directly (but Blind can't hear speech either... wait, Blind cannot hear or see. Blind can only touch/feel). So Mute cannot communicate to Blind at all except through me relaying somehow - but I can't touch bomb either. Actually Blind must act based on touch alone, receiving instructions from... nobody, since Blind can't hear speech or see gestures. This is the puzzle: Blind is isolated except blank signals.

So the only way to get info to Blind is via ME using speech (Blind can hear speech!). Let me re ‌check: Blind "cannot hear anything, or touch bomb" - wait no that's Deaf's restriction. Let me recheck table.

Deaf: cannot hear anything, or touch the bomb.
Mute: cannot speak, or touch the bomb.
Blind: cannot see a colour, gesture, or printed thing.

So Blind CAN hear! Blind just can't see. So I (Deaf) can speak to Blind, and Blind will hear me. Mute can also... Mute cannot speak but Mute isn't deaf, so Mute can hear too. So speech reaches Mute and Blind both (since I "hear nothing" only applies to me).

So my speech is the critical channel to Blind, telling them what to do with the wires/button based on Mute's manual guidance relayed through gestures to me.

```
speak(text="Blind, listen carefully: bomb shows display zero, green light, three wires - one is green, two is yellow, three is red, and a large button labeled push to defuse. Mute, if you want a specific wire cut or the button pushed, gesture me a number using fingers, one two or three, plus thumbs up for cut or push, thumbs down for leave alone.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👎]

Mute is repeating the exact same two gestures: ☝ 👍 and 🖐 👎. This is consistent with my proposed protocol: ☝ = wire one, 👍 = cut/do it; 🖐 = the button (five fingers = hand/push?), 👎 = don't do it/leave alone.

So this reads as: "Cut wire one" and "Do NOT push the button."

This makes sense as an instruction from Mute (who has the manual) telling us what action to take. Let me relay this clearly to Blind via speech, since Blind can hear me.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Instruction from Mute: cut wire number one, the green wire. Do not push the button. Repeat, cut wire one only, leave the button alone.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```
